study.title: A generative model for inorganic materials design
study.workflow_type: Unconditional and property-conditioned inorganic crystal generation with computational and experimental validation
study.assessment_scope: Published article, Supplementary Information, and data and code availability statements; released artefacts were identified but the analysis was not rerun.

items.summary: Alex-MP-20 size and selection, source versions and licences, DFT harmonisation, deduplication, and the extended ICSD novelty reference are described; split manifests, hashes, cross-split collision rates, and shortcut or perturbation checks are not reported.
source_locations: Supplementary Sections C.1-C.2 and Fig. C3

items.summary: Training-set selection, excluded experimental systems, and task-specific conditional data are described, but complete train/validation/test sizes, reusable manifests, and a study-wide account of model-selection data are not provided.
The diffusion variables, GemNet backbone, architecture, and fine-tuning method are detailed, but random seeds are not stated.

Base-model and fine-tuning steps, Adam optimisation, learning-rate rules, batch sizes, and eight A100 GPUs are specified; wall-clock distributions, numerical precision, and inference throughput are not.

Unconditional and conditional targets, classifier-free guidance, 1,000 reverse-diffusion steps, one Langevin corrector, sample counts, element masks, relaxation, and rejection procedures are specified.

Stability, uniqueness, novelty, and relaxation RMSD are defined with the evaluation stage, structure-matcher tolerances, and sensitivity analysis; uncertainty across independent generative runs is not reported for the principal metrics.
source_locations: Supplementary Sections D.3-D.4 and Table D3

items.summary: MatterGen is compared with CDVAE and DiffCSP and ablated by component. Substitution and random structure search use the same machine-learning force-field screen and a common budget of 100 DFT relaxations per chemical system.
source_locations: Supplementary Sections A.10-A.11 and Table A2
Supplementary Sections D.5.2 and D.6.1 and Table D5

items.summary: The bulk-modulus workflow separates composition filtering, machine-learning-potential stability, novelty, phonons, DFT stability, expert selection, synthesis, and measurement, and reports the complete attrition from 32,768 candidates to four synthesis attempts and one confirmed product, with synthesis conditions and failures reported separately.

Training data, model code, pretrained checkpoints, evaluation code, and data licences are linked, but no complete environment lockfile, split-file checksums, determinism record, or single rebuild command is identified.
source_locations: Main text, Data availability and Code availability

items.summary: The reported generation and down-selection workflows do not retrain the generator or acquire new labels across sequential rounds; their multi-stage screening is covered by G1, E1, and F1.
Accelerator type and count, optimisation steps, and batch sizes are reported, but training and inference wall-clock distributions, candidates per GPU-hour, and energy or carbon estimates are not.

The reported workflow targets stable inorganic crystals and does not expose a hazardous target, autonomous execution pathway, or access mechanism that makes a governance control material to the claim. Dataset licences are assessed under D1 and R1; prospective experiments are assessed under F1.
source_locations: Main text, Methods and Data availability

items.summary: The main computational sample counts and experimental attrition funnel are recoverable, but training cost, inference throughput, and one consolidated record spanning all generation tasks are not provided.

notes: This is a disclosure audit rather than a methodological quality score. No unreported detail was inferred.
